newsitem.title: ITALY: Ciampi doubts sustainability of Italian pensions.
newsitem.headline: Ciampi doubts sustainability of Italian pensions.

text.p: Italian Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said there were doubts on the sustainability of Italy's pensions system in the medium term and for this reason it was in need of reforms.

According to a summary from the Chamber of Deputies, or lower house, Ciampi told the house's budget committee that pension reforms worked out in 1995 "will probably have to be corrected. And that is what the government intends to do."
Ciampi repeated that the government's annual document of three-year rolling economic targets (DPEF) would set out its strategies for reforming the pensions system.

"The problem of the welfare state regards pensions above all. There are doubts that the pensions system even after reforms, may not be balanced in the medium term. For this reason it will be necessary to intervene," he said.

The government has placed welfare reform high on the agenda as it fights to straighten out public finances and win a place in Europe's planned currency union. But it faces opposition from trade unions and its hard-left Communist Refoundation allies to make any changes before 1998.
Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti, in a statement released after Ciampi's comments, said he supported the trade unions' stance.
